newsitem.title: UK: BZW profit rumours hurt Barclays shares.
newsitem.headline: BZW profit rumours hurt Barclays shares.

text.p: Market rumours and press reports of a collapse in profits at Barclays' investment banking unit BZW on Monday slashed 23p of the parent's share price.

Barclays shares were quoted at 1193p, down from Friday's close of 1216p, amid reports that its profit would slump to 190 million stg in 1996 from 282 million in 1995 when Barclays announces its 1996 results on Tuesday.
"I would be surprised if the fall was as dramatic as that," said John Leonard, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers. "They already have 157 million stg in the bag from the first half."
BZW has had had a turbulent time in the past year which started with the death of its chief executive David Band.

Barclays appointed Bill Harrison to replace Band and brought in Bob Diamond to be Global Markets chief last July. Around 30 people left the firm in November including the deputy markets head and the head of forex trading.

Analysts say such management turmoil which saw another senior appointment as recently as this month when Charles Stonehill was appointed Chief Executive of investment banking, is very difficult to manage successfully and it is likely that, as a house, BZW had had its eye off the ball on occasion.
But, on top of this, BZW has also been involved in some high-profile disasters with its clients.
The biggest of these was its takeover defence for British regional electricity company Northern Electric against U.S. energy group CE Electric which is being investigated by Britain's Takeover Panel.
The late disclosure by BZW of a 250,000 stg discretionary fee clause meant that CE's offer was extended and it captured Northern by the slimmest of margins.
"All the things that have been happening will have affected them," said one analyst who declined to be named, "but I also think that Barclays strategy as a commercial bank isn't helping BZW."
The analyst said the fact that Barclays as a commercial banking was cutting down its large corporate relationships makes it more difficult for BZW to win mandates.
"Barclays will say that the BZW profits fall is just a short-term blip but it won't be if the problem is coming from the customer end," he added.
Analysts say costs are an ongoing problem at BZW but that Barclays always claims it is building for the future.
Apart from the top-level hiring, BZW is adding staff and in the recent City climate, this can be expensive.
"The expense has to be justified at some point," said one analyst. "And it looks as though recently that is proving to be a bit difficult."
Analysts say they expect lower profits from BZW but would be surprised if the collapse was quite as big as some have predicted.
"If I were to be really cynical, I'd say they were softening up the market for bad news but I don't think BZW really works that way," another analyst said.
BZW declined to comment on the rumours.
